subject: English
central_question: How does Professor Gaitonde’s encounter with an alternative present connect a turning point in history with catastrophe theory, quantum uncertainty and the possibility of different realities?
in_scope_units: Professor Gaitonde travels through an unfamiliar Pune-Bombay route and discovers that British territory still exists in Bombay.
The Asiatic Society library reveals an alternative history in which the Marathas win the Battle of Panipat.
The alternate account traces political, technological and democratic consequences of the Maratha victory.
Bhausahebanchi Bakhar identifies Vishwasrao’s survival as the battle’s decisive divergence.
At Azad Maidan, Gaitonde clashes with an audience over an unoccupied presidential chair and disappears.
Back in his familiar world, a torn page provides material evidence for his experience.
Rajendra uses catastrophe theory, quantum indeterminism and transitions between possible worlds to explain the event.
The end exercises connect history, science, language, idioms, unreal conditions and popular scientific theories.
banned_topics: The adjacent travel chapter Silk Road
A claim that the alternate history is factual Indian history
Advanced quantum physics beyond Rajendra’s explanation
Scientific proof that parallel worlds or brain-triggered transitions occur

known_pitfalls.claim: The story reports a real historical discovery.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is fiction built around a real historical event and an imagined alternative result.
Professor Gaitonde is the historian; Rajendra provides the scientific explanation.
Rajendra says he remains in the present but experiences a different world with another history.

known_pitfalls.claim: The torn page scientifically proves parallel worlds.
known_pitfalls.correction: It makes Rajendra take the experience seriously within the story, but his explanation remains a theory and guess.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Maratha victory account is the history of Gaitonde’s normal world.
known_pitfalls.correction: In his familiar world Vishwasrao is hit; in the alternative world the bullet misses and the Marathas win.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with Understanding the Text I by identifying the story as fiction centred on a real historical turning point and linking history with science.
Use Understanding the Text II.1-3 for the alternative present, catastrophic experience and comparison of the two Indias.
Use Understanding the Text II.4-5 for quantum indeterminism and the need for interaction in a transition.
Use Talking About the Text Q1-Q2 for single historical events, reality, methods of inquiry and comparison with the sea adventure.
Conclude with Working with Words, Noticing Form and Things to Do on idioms, confusing word pairs, unreal conditionals, catastrophe theory and other scientific theories.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The story ends with Understanding the Text I.1-5 and II.1-5, Talking About the Text questions 1-2, Thinking About Language, Working with Words I-II, Noticing Form and two Things to Do sections.
